context:
Goal: each new lane session starts work from its brief with no pause, at the effort you want.
Problem (rule): two records say you ruled lane effort medium on 2026-10-30 15:11 CDT, and you said at 13:17 CST you never ruled it; the fixed start prompt and the guard that holds it were a coordinator build, so the records need your word to change.
Based on (read): the guard that pins a lane's start lets the tool that starts a session open a lane only when the first prompt is exactly "/effort medium".
Based on (measured): at 13:12 CST, three lanes got the same brief as a message; two acted and one paused for a grant.
Departs from: main (a lane's first prompt is exactly "/effort medium", and the brief follows as a message) — the lane starts with its effort set by the tool that starts a session and the whole brief as its first prompt, and the fixed-prompt guard goes.
Meanwhile: the coordinator holds the step that makes a lane's brief cite your grant; other lanes go on.
home: decisions agent-model-cap (The lane effort pin) and session-tiers (Lane session effort); step lane-brief-cites-grant

options.gain: A lane starts work from its brief at once, and its effort stays fixed at medium.
options.how: Lanes start with the whole brief as the first prompt and effort medium set at the start; the fixed-prompt guard goes.
options.label: Brief as first prompt, keep medium effort (Recommended if you want a fixed effort)
options.lose: A lane that needs more effort for hard work still runs at medium.

options.gain: A lane starts work from its brief at once, and its effort fits its role.
options.how: Lanes start with the whole brief as the first prompt; effort follows the table of model and effort per agent role; the fixed-prompt guard goes.
options.label: Brief as first prompt, effort by role
options.lose: Lane effort can vary, so cost per lane is less even.

options.how: Lanes keep the exact "/effort medium" first prompt; the brief stays a message; the records keep citing you.
options.label: Keep today's fixed start prompt
options.lose: Lanes can still pause on a brief that arrives as a peer message, and the records cite a ruling you say you never made.

reply: You answered this in chat at 13:19 CST, before it reached the page (relayed by the coordinator at 13:20 and 13:22 CST): "B is good". That was the coordinator's letter b, which is option a here: a lane starts with the whole brief as its first prompt, opening with a Grant line, and effort medium set at the start; the fixed-prompt guard goes. Triage builds it now, failing tests first, and the two records drop the 2026-10-30 cite and cite your 13:19 CST words. (Triage, 13:25 CST.)
title: How should a new lane session start: with its effort set and its whole brief as the first prompt, or with today's fixed start prompt?
why: Today a lane's first prompt must be exactly "/effort medium", so its brief arrives later as a message from another session; one lane paused on that at 13:12 CST as "peer message, no grant".
